title: Zesty Thai Rice Noodles
description: A vibrant Thai rice noodle dish infused with wine, pillowy noodles, and zesty gherkin relish. Energizing and low FODMAP, this dish pairs the tang of lime with the sweetness of wine.

ingredients.name: thai sweet wine
ingredients.notes: use a dry or semi-dry version

ingredients.name: tamari
ingredients.notes: low FODMAP substitute for fish sauce

instructions: Soak the kanom jeen in warm water for 5 minutes until softened, then drain and set aside.
Place a saucepan of water on low heat, add the wine, lime juice, tamari, and sriracha; bring to a gentle simmer.
Whisk the grated ginger into the sauce, then stir in the shredded carrot and gherkin relish, cooking for 2 minutes until the carrot is slightly tender.
Lower the heat to maintain a bain-marie style gentle simmer, then fold in the softened noodles and stir to combine.
Cook for 3 minutes, then remove from heat and let the mixture rest for 2 minutes for pillowy texture.
Transfer the noodles to a serving bowl, drizzle with any remaining sauce, and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and chopped cilantro.
Gently toss to distribute the flavors evenly and serve immediately, optionally adding a squeeze of lime for extra brightness.
Enjoy the zesty, winey, and energizing Thai rice noodles, perfect for a quick lunch that’s both low FODMAP and pillowy.
